Searching InvesƟgaƟon Data within Physical Sciences InformaƟcs (PSI)
    1.  InvesƟgaƟon Search Filters: Select speciﬁc Research Area(s) or Project Type(s) to narrow the list of resulƟng invesƟgaƟons based on the selected criteria.
    2.  PSI Toolbar: To navigate to the external PSI home page at anyƟme, click on the NASA logo or Home link. Click "Data & Tools" to navigate to the Submission Portal or Workspace.
    3.  Search Bar: Users can search using keywords (e.g. ethane) and Boolean operators such as “AND”, “OR”, and “NOT”. (e.g. Ethane AND N-Butane)
    4.  Results Sort: InvesƟgaƟons by default are sorted by “Release Date” but can be adjusted to reﬂect “Title” or “Accession ID”.
    5.  InvesƟgaƟon Title (Acronym): InvesƟgaƟons are displayed as a list. Clicking the Title (Acronym) redirects users to the selected invesƟgaƟon page.
    6.  Results Display: Shows the number of search results available by page. The default display is 25, but this can be adjusted to 50 or 100.

NavigaƟng a PSI InvesƟgaƟon Page
   NavigaƟon Panel
   On the leŌ of the page is the navigaƟon panel, which allows users to go directly to a speciﬁc secƟon of the invesƟgaƟon page.

   Overview
   The top of the page contains the invesƟgaƟon id (e.g. PSI-8) along with Ɵtle and acronym, assigned DOI and speciﬁcs about the invesƟgaƟons research area.
    Clicking “Cite this InvesƟgaƟon” generates the downloadable citaƟon that should be used when referencing this invesƟgaƟon in published materials.

InvesƟgaƟon DescripƟon SecƟon
This secƟon contains general details (e.g. Project Type, Start & End Date, etc), the speciﬁc ObjecƟves, Approach, Hypothesis and Beneﬁts, as well as invesƟgaƟon contact informaƟon.

Experiment Table
The secƟon for the Experiment Table provides speciﬁc details on the invesƟgaƟon samples and runs. This table is also available to download in the “Data Files and documents” secƟon.





Hardware
Hardware and experiment facility informaƟon is available as clickable external link(s) in the “Hardware” secƟon.

RepresentaƟve Images
Thumbnails of science and/or other invesƟgaƟon related images idenƟﬁed by PIs appear in this secƟon. Users can navigate through mulƟple images using the arrow butons on either side of the image.

Data Files and Documents
The ﬁles secƟon provides users with access to invesƟgaƟon dataﬁles and supporƟng documentaƟon. Files are organized into separate folders based on ﬁle type. Raw and Analyzed Data
folders are addiƟonally separated by Reduced or Earth gravity. AddiƟonal data subfolders may be present depending on the speciﬁc invesƟgaƟon.

To download a speciﬁc ﬁle or an enƟre folder, select the corresponding checkbox and click “download” to either view the ﬁle in a new window or save it to your local device.
More information on downloading large files or large quantities of files is available in the next section of this guide.

blocks.text: Overview
Feature Details
Download Large Files  (Over 1GB)
This feature allows you to download multiple large files from the data repository.
Large downloads are automatically prepared in multiple parts and delivered to your email for easier access.

-
Estimated size: total estimated size of the selected files
-
Files selected: number of files selected
-
Part size: total files will divided into part size of maximum 15GB
-
Retention: number of days the shared download link will be remain valid
-
Email address: email address where the download link will be sent
-
Acknowledgement multiple parts delivery: confirmation that large files may be delivered in multiple parts
When you select files larger than 1GB and click the Download Zip button, a new Prepare large download section will appear with the following details:

blocks.text: Best Practices

-
Ensure stable internet: use reliable connection to avoid errors.

-
Avoid errors: save all files in the same folder before extracting.
-
Download promptly: links expire after the retention period. Save the files before they are no longer available.

-
Select files wisely: download only the files you need to reduce processing time. For very large datasets, consider 
splitting them into smaller batches.
-
Manage multi-part downloads: avoid running multiple large downloads at once for better performance.

-
Use reliable email address: double-check for email typos and verify spam folder/filter in you haven’t received any 
email.
